description.purpose: A document in a turn becomes a file of this space (GH #907): the turn's first attachment `{blob_id, mime_type, filename, size_bytes, sha256}` -- a pointer into the colony's blob store -- is born under `/inbox/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<name>` (a taken name gets ` (2)`, ` (3)`, ...), a PDF with one `derived` text page per page, and the turn goes on as `turn` without `attachments` and with one text turn after the caption: `[file fh-<id>@<v12> "<name>", <n> pages: <oneline>]`. It never reads the bytes; the model reads the address.
description.use_when: Reached on `in_ingest` of the hive path, which a member draws for a turn whose channel set `hop.has_file`. It hands the reference on: a PDF to `./extract` (which reads the blob and sends the `create` to `./write`), any other document as a `create` on `in_write` with `args.attachment` 0, caller `ingest`, `notify`. It searches again on `path_taken` and waits for `./derive`'s `derived`, then counts the file's `derived` parts for the line.
description.not_in_scope: No reading of the blob (it does not declare `consumes.body.attachments`), no second file per turn (only the first attachment is born), no sorting out of the inbox (the owner's or a later wave's `move`), no bytes or page text in any row, hop, context or turn it hands on.
description.emits_meaning: turn: the turn it received, hop keys kept, `attachments` removed, the address line or -- when the file could not be born -- `[file "<name>" could not be stored: <code>]` as one text turn after the caption; a turn is never swallowed. The other routes are its own calls: `ingest_store` (its parked rows -- the request with the reference, a claim on the name -- the path lookup and the page count), `in_extract` (`{attachments: [ref], path, mime}` for a PDF), `in_write` (`create`, caller `ingest`, notify '1', `args.attachment` 0, `attachments: [ref]`).
description.consumes_meaning: body.messages and body.attachments: the turn; only the first attachment is born, as a reference (the blob is never read here). Answers come back as `answer` (op_id, caller `ingest`) and `derived` (file, caller `ingest`).
